artifact.title: Packing performance

kpis.label: Boxes packed
kpis.definition: PACK_COMPLETED scans on the PACK station for the scope, on the selected PST day.

kpis.label: Earned minutes
kpis.definition: Standard minutes the work was worth: 5 small, 15 medium, 60 big per box, or the per-SKU estimate when the operator has profiled it.

kpis.label: Handle minutes
kpis.definition: Clock time from each PACK_SCAN to its matching PACK_COMPLETED, summed. Unpaired completions contribute nothing.

kpis.label: Wait minutes
kpis.definition: Idle time between boxes: previous completion to the next scan, clamped at zero, gaps over 90 min excluded as breaks. Verdict is on wait per box (3m).

kpis.label: Efficiency
kpis.definition: Earned minutes ÷ handle minutes. Over 100% means the floor beat the pack standard.

kpis.label: Utilization
kpis.definition: Handle minutes ÷ attended minutes (first scan to last completion). Low utilization is a feeding problem, not a packer problem.

kpis.label: Minutes per box
kpis.definition: Handle minutes ÷ boxes packed. Compare against the tier mix before reading it as a pace.

kpis.label: Capacity left
kpis.definition: Workday minutes minus handle minutes for this packer.

sections.title: Per packer
sections.note: Earned is standard minutes for the tier mix; handle is scan-to-complete clock time.

sections.title: Item number to time
sections.note: Newest first, one row per completed pack scan (max 200).

artifact.title: Unbox backlog
artifact.question: How many boxes are left to be unboxed?
artifact.scope: Receiving · cartons in the building, not yet unboxed

kpis.label: Boxes waiting
kpis.definition: Cartons (receiving_carton rows) with a triage door scan or a receiving scan whose receiving_unbox.unboxed_at is still NULL. One row = one physical box.

kpis.label: Units waiting
kpis.definition: SUM(receiving_line.quantity_expected) across the lines on those cartons. A line with no expected quantity contributes 0, so this is a floor, not a guess.

kpis.label: Oldest box
kpis.definition: Whole calendar days in America/Los_Angeles since COALESCE(door_received_at, receiving_date_time, created_at) on the oldest waiting carton. Good ≤ 2 days, watch ≤ 5.

kpis.label: On the bench
kpis.definition: Waiting cartons with receiving_unbox.opened_at set but unboxed_at still NULL — opened on the bench and abandoned half-done. Close these out first: the box is already open.

kpis.label: Returns
kpis.definition: Waiting cartons flagged receiving_carton.is_return.

kpis.label: Priority
kpis.definition: Waiting cartons flagged receiving_carton.is_priority — the shared unbox/test urgency flag (tier 0 or a manual toggle).

kpis.label: Unfound
kpis.definition: Waiting cartons whose receiving_triage.pairing_state = 'UNFOUND' — no purchase order matched, so they cannot be received against a PO until someone identifies them.

sections.title: Age of the backlog
sections.note: Whole calendar days since the carton arrived, in America/Los_Angeles.

sections.title: Where it came from
sections.note: receiving_carton.source — how the carton entered the building.

standards.label: Bucket · Today
standards.note: Whole calendar days in America/Los_Angeles between the arrival date and today.

standards.label: Backlog predicate
standards.note: A carton counts when it has a triage door scan or a receiving scan, and receiving_unbox.unboxed_at is still NULL.

standards.label: Arrival timestamp
standards.note: Age is measured from COALESCE(receiving_triage.door_received_at, receiving_carton.receiving_date_time, receiving_carton.created_at).

notes: Left to be unboxed = a carton that arrived (triage door scan, or at least one receiving scan) and whose unbox milestone is unstamped (receiving_unbox.unboxed_at IS NULL). Same predicate as the triage "to unbox" queue, so this count matches the bench.
A carton is ONE physical box, not one item. Units are SUM(receiving_line.quantity_expected) across the lines on the carton; a line with no expected quantity counts as 0.
There is no weight or dimension column on a carton, so this report offers no volume, tonnage or "how long will it take" estimate. Sizing the pile is done by box count and units only.

Blind spot: a carrier-delivered package that was never scanned at the dock is physically here but NOT in this count — nothing recorded its arrival. That hunt is the delivered-but-unscanned queue at /api/receiving-lines/incoming/delivered-unscanned.

headline.label: Most expensive order in the building

kpis.label: Top order value
kpis.definition: SUM(orders.sale_amount) over every line sharing this orders.order_id, among orders still in the building. Sale price, not margin.

kpis.label: Top order age
kpis.definition: Whole days between now and COALESCE(orders.order_date, orders.created_at) on the top order, taking the oldest of its lines. Good ≤ 2 days, watch ≤ 5.

kpis.label: Top order stage
kpis.definition: The least advanced line on the top order: AWAITING_LABEL (no shipment), BLOCKED (out of stock), PENDING, PICKED (tech scan or serial) or PACKED (pack scan).

kpis.label: Orders in building
kpis.definition: Distinct orders.order_id groups passing all four "still here" clauses: no SHIP_CONFIRM, no carrier custody, not AFN, not caged without a catalog SKU.

kpis.label: Value in building
kpis.definition: SUM(orders.sale_amount) across every line of every order still in the building. This is SALE value at risk of sitting, not margin — no cost or fee column exists.

kpis.label: Past ship-by value
kpis.definition: Sale value of orders whose earliest ORDER/TEST work_assignments.deadline_at is already in the past. Any dollar past due reads bad.

sections.title: Top orders by value
sections.note: Ranked by SUM(sale_amount) over the lines of each order_id. Sale price, not margin.

sections.title: Lines in the top order
sections.note: Every line still in the building on order 11-12874-40012.

rows.product: Bose Acoustimass 10 Series V speaker system

sections.title: Value by stage
sections.note: An order's stage is its least advanced line — one held line holds the order.

standards.label: Not scanned out
standards.note: The order's shipment has no station_activity_logs row with activity_type = 'SHIP_CONFIRM' — nobody scanned it out at the dock.

standards.label: Not in carrier custody
standards.note: shipping_tracking_numbers shows no acceptance, transit, out-for-delivery or delivery, and no latest_status_category beyond LABEL_CREATED or UNKNOWN.

standards.label: Not Amazon-fulfilled
standards.note: AFN/FBA orders are shipped by Amazon, so they are never physically here.

standards.label: Not caged without a SKU
standards.note: A caged row with no sku_catalog_id is a gated placeholder, not stock standing on the floor.

notes: Order value is SUM(orders.sale_amount) over every row sharing the same orders.order_id — `orders` is a line table, so one row is one line, not one order.
This is SALE price, not profit. There is no cost, fee or margin column on orders, so no margin, no landed cost and no net figure is computed or implied anywhere on this report.
Amazon-fulfilled orders (fulfillment_channel = AFN) are excluded: Amazon picks, packs and ships those, so they are not sitting in this warehouse.
Ship-by is not a column on orders. It is work_assignments.deadline_at for the ORDER/TEST assignment on the order row — the earliest such deadline when the order has several lines.
An order's stage is its LEAST advanced line (AWAITING_LABEL → BLOCKED → PENDING → PICKED → PACKED), because one unlabeled or out-of-stock line holds the whole order.

rows.why: Inventory that arrived, got put away, and never reached a channel earns nothing while it ages.
Stock nothing has moved in a quarter is carrying cost with no demand signal behind it.
A hold with no disposition is a decision nobody has made yet.
A carton stuck in receiving exception never becomes sellable inventory.
Labour and parts are already sunk into these; unfinished means the spend has not converted.
Every open exception is an order a customer is waiting on that no station is working.

sections.title: Effort to clear
sections.note: Minutes-per-unit are declared standards; person-days divide by a 480-minute workday.

standards.label: Priority formula
standards.note: priority = units × ageWeight, where ageWeight = 1 + min(oldestDays, 60) / 30 (0 days = 1.0x, 30 days = 2.0x, 60+ days = 3.0x, capped)

notes: Every number in the Stuck column is a LIVE row count from the table named in the gap — never an estimate, never a model guess.

NO dollar figure is attached to any gap. This schema carries no reliable per-unit price, so a revenue ranking would be invented; effort and age are declared or measured, and are what the ranking uses instead.
The minutes-per-unit figures are declared operating standards, not measurements. Change one and the ranking changes — that is the point of printing them.
A gap is a CATEGORY, not a work order. Use the follow-up question under a gap to pull the actual rows before assigning anyone.
Person-days divide total effort by a 480-minute workday from org_pack_capacity.workday_minutes.

headline.label: Best first delegation
headline.hint: Received but never listed · TECH · 7h 20m free

kpis.label: Send first
kpis.definition: The eligible staffer with the most free capacity for the top gap's station (TECH). Eligibility is staff_stations, with an employee_id prefix fallback.

kpis.label: Their free capacity
kpis.definition: 480-minute workday minus 20 minutes per pending task. Good at half a day or better; bad once the assumed load fills the day.

kpis.label: Top gap
kpis.definition: The highest-priority gap from the ROI ranking (units × ageWeight), cleared by the station in the declared gap→station map.

kpis.label: Eligible on TECH
kpis.definition: Active staff whose stations include TECH. One deep is a single point of failure; zero means the station is unstaffed.

kpis.label: Roster pending
kpis.definition: All pending floor assignments plus desk tasks currently owned by an active staffer.

kpis.label: Unowned pending
kpis.definition: Pending floor and desk work with a NULL assignee — NOBODY owns these, so nobody will finish them.

kpis.label: Most loaded
kpis.definition: The active staffer holding the most pending tasks across floor and desk. Do not stack the top gap here.

sections.title: Who to send at the top 3 gaps
sections.note: Staff listed least-loaded first, by free capacity. Eligibility comes from the declared gap→station map.

sections.title: Roster load
sections.note: Active staff only. Free = 480 min − 20 min per pending task.

sections.title: Unowned pending work
sections.note: Pending items with a NULL assignee, floor first. Desk rows carry no priority — ops_plan_tasks has no priority column.

standards.label: Minutes per pending task
standards.note: ASSUMPTION, not a measurement — neither work_assignments nor ops_plan_tasks records an expected duration.

standards.label: Workday
standards.note: org_pack_capacity.workday_minutes, or the 480-minute default when unset.

standards.label: Free capacity formula
standards.note: free_minutes = workday_minutes − (pending_tasks × ASSUMED_MINUTES_PER_TASK). Pending = floor work OPEN/ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS plus desk tasks open/in_progress.

standards.label: Gap → station
standards.note: unlisted_units→TECH, dead_stock→SALES, open_order_exceptions→PACK, open_receiving_exceptions→UNBOX, units_on_hold→TECH, repairs_in_flight→TECH

notes: free_minutes is capacity MINUS an assumed 20 minutes per pending task. That 20 is an assumption, printed here so it can be argued with — no table in this schema records a per-task duration.
Station eligibility comes from staff_stations. 1 staffer has no staff_stations row, so their station was DERIVED from the employee_id prefix and is marked "(derived)".
Delegating is a human action. This report names WHO; the assignment itself is made with the existing verb, POST /api/tasks (permission work_orders.claim), which this report does not call.
ops_plan_tasks has no priority column, so desk urgency comes from due_at only: "urgent" means due within a day, "overdue" means already past.
Gap counts are live row counts from the ROI ranking (units × ageWeight); no dollar value is attached to any of them.
